input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now calls stats.clear() on a single dict shared by every invocation of the decorated function, instead of giving each call its own statistics dict. Concurrent calls from different threads then wipe each other's in-flight statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two threads call the same @retry-decorated function at the same time. Mechanism: the second call's stats.clear() on line 377 resets the dict that the first call is still updating, and both calls write into that one dict. Impact: the statistics that wrapped_f.statistics reports for either call are wrong or incomplete, which the original rebinding avoided.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label. A single statistics dict is shared across invocations and reset with stats.clear(), so concurrent calls wipe each other's in-flight stats and the reported statistics end up wrong. It covers the threading case explicitly, which the label lists as one failure path.
